page: Amazon Web Services c6g.large is an entry-level compute-optimized instance powered by AWS Graviton2 processors built on the 64-bit ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 architecture. Operating on the AWS Nitro System, the instance provides 2 dedicated physical cores running at 2.5 GHz without simultaneous multithreading, paired with 4.0 GB of system memory. Cache configuration includes 64 KB of L1 data cache and 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, alongside a shared 32 MB L3 cache. The instance relies entirely on remote storage, offering no local bundled NVMe drives, and includes a baseline network throughput of 1 Gbps without bundled public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations position the c6g.large in the middle tier for stress-ng single-core processing with a score of 1519.49, while multi-core compute throughput reflects its modest two-core footprint at 3010.97. Memory performance registers uncached read bandwidth of 38.93 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 18.73 GB/sec. Application benchmarks indicate capable entry-level throughput, yielding 2.28 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 2.39 GB/sec in static web serving, though heavy multi-core compiling and complex calculations exhibit lower aggregate throughput.

The 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio delivers cost-efficient, dedicated compute capacity for applications ported to arm64. The primary tradeoff stems from its small resource envelope and reliance on network-attached storage, limiting its effectiveness for data-heavy analytics. The c6g.large is suited for lightweight microservices, front-end web servers, containerized application tasks, small-scale caching layers, and continuous integration runners adapted to the ARM instruction set.
description: Amazon Web Services c6g.large is an arm64 compute-optimized instance powered by a 2.5 GHz AWS Graviton2 Neoverse-N1 processor under the Nitro System. It features 2 dedicated physical vCPUs without simultaneous multithreading, 4.0 GB of system memory (2.0 GB per vCPU), and hardware AES encryption. The instance provisions no local ephemeral storage and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps. In benchmark tests, the instance demonstrates average single-core CPU execution alongside 2.28 million Redis SET operations per second and 2.39 GB/sec static web throughput, constrained primarily by its small dual-core capacity and moderate uncached memory bandwidth. Operating with a lean 1:2 core-to-memory ratio, the c6g.large offers efficient dedicated compute resource utilization without hyperthreading overhead. It is well suited for lightweight arm64 workloads, including distributed microservices, low-traffic web serving, small caching layers, and containerized CI/CD build environments.
